# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 49 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Mich. 130, Shepherd of Hermas 49 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_049_page_001.jpg

---

## Council Notes

Chapter 49 closes the Mandates with a solemn authority statement. The Shepherd claims not merely angelic authority but divine authority: "these are not the words of a human being but of the Lord God." This is an extraordinary claim — the Shepherd positions himself as speaking with full divine commission.

The phrase "life in the age to come" (*zōēn eis ton aiōna ton erchomenon*) is eschatological — Hermas uses apocalyptic reward language familiar from Jewish-Christian tradition. The binary of good desire leading to life and evil desire to death recapitulates the Two Ways tradition (Didache 1-6; Barnabas 18-20).

EMET closes with "Keep them and you shall live" — LOGOS agrees. This is a consciously Deuteronomic formula (Deut 8:1: "all the commandment...you shall be careful to do, that you may live"). Hermas presents his Twelve Commandments with the weight of the Torah.

---

## Mandate 12, Part 6 — The Twelve Commandments

**49:1** "These twelve commandments, O Hermas, are to be kept and observed. But above all keep faith. For if you maintain faith you will be able to keep all these things. And I will show you who are the ministers of these commandments, so that you may know that I am adding nothing of my own here, but that these are truly the commandments of God."

**49:2** "The twelve commandments are to be kept. When the man who has faith in the Lord keeps these commandments, he will receive from the Lord a great reward — even life in the age to come. But the man who does not keep them will die the death, for his deeds do not permit him to live."

**49:3** "All those who hold fast to evil desire will remain in the wretched state in which they find themselves. But those who renounce evil desire and clothe themselves with good desire will receive life from the Lord, for every good desire leads to life and every evil desire leads to death."

**49:4** "Further, I say to you: hold fast to the good desire and keep it, lest it depart from you. For it is strong and of great power. Keep it with all your strength, for it will bring you to life. But if you hold to evil desire, know that it will lead you to death, as I have already shown you."

**49:5** "The twelve commandments were given for this reason, O Hermas — that you might understand that these words are from me and are not the words of a human being but of the Lord God. I have the authority to give such commandments. Keep them and you shall live."

---

*SOPHIA represents the consensus rendering of EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA, with rulings recorded in the Disagreement Log.*
